h1: Data Signal — AI & SaaS Landing Page Design
tagline: Landing page reference built around “Abstract red and blue smoke”, with the layout, timings and palette written down in the brief.
summary: Landing page reference for an AI or SaaS product — 520ms transitions, cubic-bezier(.16,1.3,1) easing, #050606 base and Inter.
about: This is the landing page from Data Signal, published with the brief that produced it rather than as a screenshot. The page's own headline reads “Abstract red and blue smoke”, and the composition is built around those exact words. The colour scheme is deep teal #050606 underneath and white #EDEDED for the type, and the page is set in Inter. Delivery is one self-contained HTML file, captured at 1482x1080 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. The page keeps its motion to 520ms transitions, cubic-bezier(.16,1.3,1) and a looping video bed. Keep it open while you write: the 12,007-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: A navigation bar that gets out of the way
layout.body: The bar overlays the landing page instead of pushing it down, so the composition keeps the full height of the first screen. Labels are short enough to fit one line at 619px, and the active item is marked with weight rather than with a pill. Keep the link count to four or five; the row is sized for that.

layout.title: Media without an overlay
layout.body: Video sits on the bottom layer of the 1482x1080 composition, with the type arranged above it and nothing in between. The loop is short enough (5.9s) that the eye reads it as texture rather than as a timeline.

layout.title: The announcement pill
layout.body: One badge, one message: the pill sits above the headline in Inter at the smallest step, and nothing else competes for that slot. There is one announcement only, which is what makes the badge feel like news. One badge, one message.

layout.title: Navigation without a background
layout.body: The bar is a handful of elements, so it rebuilds without a component library. The reference was captured at 1482x1080.

motion.title: The loop does the ambient work
motion.body: Ambient movement is one 5.9s clip at 1482x1080, looping quietly behind the copy rather than reacting to the pointer. The clip is muted and inline, so the first frame is available without an interaction.

motion.title: Pointers only where they help
motion.body: States are handled per component (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card) rather than by a global animation layer. The states are named in the brief, so the page does not depend on a hover-effect library.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over deep teal #050606, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.
notes: Corner treatment is specified in the brief: 7px.
Panels and controls share the same corner treatment (7px), so the page keeps one surface language.
Transitions are specified at 520ms, which is the value to keep when the palette changes.

editorial.title: What to change first in Data Signal
editorial.body: If your brand runs a heavier palette, test it against the frame before you commit. deep teal #050606 carries the page, so a darker accent needs more contrast than the reference uses. Rewrite the copy and the media before you re-colour anything.

editorial.title: What an AI or SaaS product gains here
editorial.body: The claim is made once, at display size. “Abstract red and blue smoke” is doing that work from the first frame. Everything else in the landing page is ordered around that line: navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the card grid, and no second promise competes for the first read. Data Signal states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: The timing behind the landing page
editorial.body: A preset animation pack would have been quicker to ship. The brief specifies 520ms transitions, a 5.9s media loop and hover and press states instead, which is why the page reads as authored rather than staged. Nothing animates for its own sake in this landing page.

faq.question: Why does the entry name one self-contained HTML file at all?
faq.answer: Data Signal was built in one self-contained HTML file, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: What do I get when I copy the Data Signal brief?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 12,007 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: How much of Data Signal is animated?
faq.answer: Transitions are attached to interface states rather than to a scroll timeline, and they resolve in the 520ms range on cubic-bezier(.16,1.3,1). The brief records the values so a port can match them without guessing.
